concepts.name: async / await (asyncio)
concepts.explanation: Lets one program wait on many network calls at once. Python needs an explicit event loop (asyncio.run), and any blocking call inside async code stalls everything.
concepts.why: LLM apps are I/O-bound: concurrency turns a 6-minute eval into seconds.
concepts.evidenceNote: Commit 68eb58a has no AI co-author line: you discovered that urlopen and time.sleep blocked the loop and fixed the whole call chain.
concepts.example: call_tool → asyncio.to_thread(urlopen); asyncio.sleep for backoff.
concepts.gaps: A truly async client (httpx) instead of threads; TaskGroup; cancellation.
concepts.next: Swap urllib for httpx.AsyncClient and verify results match the cached run.

concepts.name: Concurrency limits (asyncio.Semaphore)
concepts.explanation: A counter that caps how many tasks run at once.
concepts.why: Stay inside API rate limits while still running concurrently.
concepts.example: rag_eval.py fans out questions with gather under a semaphore cap.
concepts.gaps: Retry-After handling, token-bucket limits.
concepts.next: Log 429s during a full run and tune the cap.

concepts.name: Rate limiting & backoff

concepts.name: Webhooks & HMAC signature verification

concepts.explanation: Running an operation twice has the same effect as once.
concepts.why: Retries and schedules must not create duplicates.

concepts.name: TLS verification (certifi)
concepts.explanation: On CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED, install a correct CA bundle — never disable verification.
concepts.why: verify=False turns a loud failure into a silent one; a red flag in reviewed code.
concepts.example: llm.py verifies TLS with certifi's bundle (commit eb536ca).

concepts.name: Lock-free ring buffer / shared memory
concepts.explanation: A fixed circular buffer one writer and one reader share without locks, here via shm_open.
concepts.why: Low-latency IPC between a privileged producer and an app.
concepts.example: AccelRingBuffer writer (daemon) / reader (app) over shm_open.

concepts.name: Privilege separation
concepts.explanation: Only the smallest component runs with elevated rights.
concepts.why: Limits blast radius.
concepts.example: Root daemon reads the sensor; the app stays unprivileged.

concepts.name: Signal fusion
concepts.explanation: Combine two noisy signals (cadence proxy + accelerometer peak) into one estimate, falling back gracefully.
concepts.why: Real sensors are messy and sometimes missing.
concepts.example: IntensityFusion blends accelerometer peaks with cadence intensity.

concepts.name: AppleScript automation
concepts.explanation: Script macOS apps (Music.app) via osascript.
concepts.why: Quick local integrations; does not survive as a hosted service.

concepts.explanation: Read heterogeneous tabular files and map them to one schema (types, dates, signs).
concepts.why: Most real ingestion starts here.

concepts.explanation: Hash a file's bytes; same hash = same file.
concepts.why: Prevents double imports.

concepts.explanation: Extract raw data, Transform it into a clean consistent shape, Load it into storage — rerunnable.

concepts.name: Chunk metadata
concepts.explanation: Title, section, URL (and game) carried on every chunk.
concepts.why: Enables citations and filtering.

concepts.name: Structured vs unstructured data
concepts.explanation: Key-value facts (an infobox) vs prose.
concepts.why: Structured facts answer the most common questions exactly.

concepts.explanation: Check your own inputs (and test data) before trusting results computed from them.

concepts.explanation: An audit log must not lose its identifiers when the subject is deleted (no ON DELETE SET NULL).

concepts.explanation: Export only the fields the analysis needs.
concepts.why: Guest names/phones never needed for ranking metrics.

concepts.name: Privacy-preserving telemetry
concepts.explanation: Log features (category, timing) not content (characters).

concepts.name: Content licenses & access terms (CC BY-NC-SA)
concepts.explanation: License governs reuse of text (credit, share-alike, non-commercial); access terms govern scripts — they are separate questions.
concepts.why: Decides whether a project can ever ship commercially.

concepts.name: Incremental indexing
concepts.explanation: Re-embed only pages that changed since the last run.
concepts.why: Keeps launch-week updates fast and cheap.

concepts.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
concepts.explanation: Two separate steps: retrieve the relevant text for a question, then give it to the model to answer from. Most failures happen in retrieval.
concepts.why: The standard way to make an LLM answer about data it was not trained on.
concepts.example: codebase-rag end to end; Tavo FAQ branch puts all facts in the prompt because the corpus is tiny.
concepts.gaps: Building one from an empty file in Python (GTA cheatsheet).

concepts.name: Chunking & overlap
concepts.explanation: Cut documents into retrievable pieces; overlap keeps ideas that straddle a boundary intact.
concepts.why: Too big buries the answer; too small loses context.
concepts.evidenceNote: make_chunks (section-bounded paragraph packing) written by you in cheatsheet.py.
concepts.example: 60-line windows with 15 overlap won every metric in a 20–100 sweep.
concepts.gaps: Structure-aware chunking (by function / section).

concepts.name: BM25 (lexical ranking)
concepts.explanation: Counts shared words with three corrections: idf (rare words matter more), k1 (repeat saturation), b (length normalization).
concepts.why: Strong, free baseline; half of every hybrid system.
concepts.example: lexical.py (~20 lines of scoring); wins on exact identifiers like merge.proximityWeight.
concepts.gaps: Derive the formula by hand.
concepts.next: Write a pytest for idf on a 3-document corpus (Task 2).

concepts.name: Keyword (lexical) search
concepts.explanation: Match on exact words.
concepts.why: Baseline that embeddings must beat.
concepts.example: keyword_search scores distinct query words found in title + section + text.
concepts.gaps: Substring matching ("car" hits "Carbonizzare"); no idf — compare with BM25 later.

concepts.name: Tokenization (incl. code identifiers)
concepts.explanation: Splitting text into units. In code, relocateToZoneId is one opaque token unless camelCase/snake_case is split. LLM tokens are a related but different idea (sub-word units that drive cost and context limits).
concepts.why: Retrieval quality and token cost both depend on it.
concepts.example: Tokenizer emits the whole identifier and its parts.
concepts.gaps: LLM sub-word tokenization and token accounting.
concepts.next: Count tokens for one codebase-rag prompt and compute its cost.

concepts.name: Stopwords
concepts.explanation: Very common words (the, is) often removed as noise.
concepts.why: Shows how a tweak can compensate for a defect elsewhere: +0.0% once the corpus was cleaned.
concepts.example: Stopword removal: +0.0%, p = 1.000 after the corpus was cleaned.

concepts.name: Embeddings & dense retrieval
concepts.explanation: Text becomes a vector; similar meaning = nearby vectors (cosine similarity after normalization).
concepts.why: Catches paraphrases keyword search misses.
concepts.example: bge-small-en-v1.5 in codebase-rag; multilingual MiniLM via @xenova/transformers in Tavo rag-practice.mjs.
concepts.gaps: Dense alone did not beat BM25 here — know why.

concepts.name: Asymmetric embedding models (query prefix)
concepts.explanation: Some models (bge) expect an instruction prefix on queries but not documents.
concepts.why: Skipping it leaves accuracy on the table.

concepts.name: Embedding model context window

concepts.name: Vector databases (pgvector)
concepts.explanation: Stores built to find nearest vectors fast; pgvector does it inside Postgres.

concepts.name: Hybrid search & Reciprocal Rank Fusion
concepts.explanation: Run keyword and vector search, merge by rank: score = Σ 1/(k + rank). Uses ranks because BM25 and cosine scores have no common scale.
concepts.why: Exact names and loose phrasing both work.

concepts.name: Derived-document pollution
concepts.explanation: Docs written about the code (agent instructions, reports) out-compete the code itself for lexical matches.

concepts.name: Prompt versioning
concepts.explanation: Prompts live as named versions and are never edited in place, so comparisons stay valid.

concepts.name: Structured output via tool calling
concepts.explanation: Define a tool with an input schema (and enums) and force the model to call it — the model can't return values outside the list.
concepts.why: Your code can check the output instead of trusting free text.

concepts.name: Truncated tool calls (max_tokens)
concepts.explanation: A tool call cut off by the token cap yields a partial input; schema "required" fields don't prevent it.
concepts.why: Never cache or trust a partial result.

concepts.name: Safe defaults on model failure
concepts.explanation: Every model failure falls back to behaviour that is no worse than before the model existed.

concepts.name: Templates vs free generation

concepts.name: Intent classification / routing

concepts.why: Basic building block of agents and assistants.

concepts.name: Multi-turn conversation state
concepts.explanation: Each webhook call is stateless, so the draft and transcript are persisted between messages.

concepts.explanation: Cache results keyed on exact inputs; unchanged prompts are free, changed ones are clean misses.

concepts.name: Hallucination

concepts.explanation: A standard protocol for exposing tools and data to AI clients; you write a server, clients call its tools.

concepts.name: Vocabulary leak in eval questions
concepts.explanation: A question that reuses the identifier it's looking for measures string matching, not retrieval.

concepts.name: recall@k
concepts.explanation: Share of questions whose correct source appears in the top k results.
concepts.why: If retrieval misses, no prompt can save the answer. But it says nothing about the other k−1 results.

concepts.name: precision@k
concepts.explanation: Of the k results, how many are relevant — "how much junk did I drag in?"
concepts.why: Noise in context can mislead the generator.
concepts.example: precision@5 ≈ 15% means roughly one useful chunk in five.

concepts.name: Mean Reciprocal Rank
concepts.explanation: Average of 1/rank of the first correct result.
concepts.why: One number that captures how high the answer appears.
concepts.example: Tavo scorer MRR 0.889; hybrid MRR 0.474 dev.

concepts.name: Ranking evaluation (top-k accuracy)
concepts.explanation: Recover where the accepted option sat in the ranked list instead of a single overridden flag.
concepts.why: Separates "near miss in ordering" from "never offered".

concepts.name: Dev / test split (held-out evaluation)
concepts.explanation: Tune on dev; confirm a decision once on test. Peeking repeatedly turns test into a second dev set.
concepts.why: Twice in codebase-rag the held-out half overturned a dev-half conclusion.
concepts.example: Dense retrieval: +14.3% recall@5 on dev, −6.0% on test — the held-out half caught it.

concepts.name: LLM-as-judge
concepts.explanation: A model grades outputs against a rubric. Safer when correctness and groundedness are separate calls, the judge is blind to the variant, and reasons before its verdict.
concepts.why: Scales answer evaluation.
concepts.example: judge.py: correctness and groundedness as two blind calls, reason field before verdict.
concepts.gaps: Using a stronger judge than the generator; agreement statistics.

concepts.name: Judge calibration (human audit)
concepts.explanation: Read a sample of the judge's verdicts by hand before trusting its numbers — including cases it passed.
concepts.why: The audit caught a rubric bug that punished honest refusals.

concepts.name: Inter-annotator agreement
concepts.explanation: How often two humans label the same item the same way.
concepts.why: If humans disagree, the system can't be held to one answer.
concepts.example: seating-003 had two valid readings and was redefined.

concepts.name: Groundedness
concepts.explanation: Is every claim in the answer supported by the retrieved text? Different from correctness.
concepts.why: Central metric for generation; hybrid lowered it on both halves.

concepts.name: Paired comparison & McNemar's test
concepts.explanation: Compare two systems on the same questions; only the questions that flip carry information. With N one-directional flips, p = 2 × 0.5^N.
concepts.why: Stops you shipping noise.
concepts.example: Hybrid vs BM25 end to end on dev: 7 gains, 7 losses on failures → p = 1.000; derived-doc exclusion: 10 gained, 0 lost → p = 0.002.

concepts.name: Statistical power & sample size

concepts.name: Multiple comparisons (Bonferroni)
concepts.explanation: Testing 4 metrics at α=0.05 gives ~19% chance of a false positive; divide α by the number of tests.
concepts.why: Only p = 0.002 survives in codebase-rag.
concepts.example: Only recall@1 at p = 0.002 survives Bonferroni (0.05/4 = 0.0125); results at p = 0.021–0.031 rest on replication.
concepts.gaps: Not yet shown unaided: explain it out loud without notes (or in an interview answer) before marking it "Independently understood".

concepts.name: Transition matrices
concepts.explanation: Cross-tab of verdicts before vs after a change.
concepts.why: Shows "+4 correct" was 8 gains and 4 losses — churn, not lift.
concepts.example: BM25→hybrid: 8 questions improved, 4 got worse — "+4 correct" was churn.

concepts.name: Composition shift
concepts.explanation: When a change alters who is in a group, that group's rate isn't comparable across runs.
concepts.why: Prevents the false conclusion that the generator got worse.
